gaps.sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.

gaps.sentence: They managed to ___ the champions in the final.
gaps.explanation: 'Beat' takes the opponent as object (beat the champions); 'win' takes the game or prize.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

gaps.sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
gaps.explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: He ___ that he would be late.
gaps.hint: '___ that ...' without a listener as object
gaps.explanation: 'Say' is used with reported content ('say that ...') without a person object; 'tell' needs one (tell me that ...).

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.
